To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fetus with IUGR is capable of increasing protein accretion by increasing amino acid delivery to the fetus and that insulin infusion does not increase protein accretion.
the fetal sheep with IUGR has suppressed protein breakdown, which increases net fetal protein accertion.
amino acids are important for fetal protein accretions in IUGR fetes and that amino acid supplementation is a potential treatment for IUGR fetues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the regulation of fetal growth and development in the normal and compromised fetus.
understanding the role of amino acids and insulin on fetal growth in the context of intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR).
understanding the regulation of protein turnover in fetal sheep during normal and abnormal growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IUGR fetus has the capacity to increase protein accretion when given an acute infusion of amino acids but not insulin.
amino acid supplementation in IUGR fetes increases net protein acccretion rates, whereas insulin supplementation does not.
the fetus can increase leucine oxidation to meet the increased amino acid supply and can also increase net protein accretions rates in response to increased amino acid supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IUGR fetusexhibit a fetal metabolic adaptation to compensate for the reduced amino acid availability.
amino acids are a key factor that regulates protein turnover and accretion in fetal life and in IUGR.
amino acid supplementation to the fetus is an effective strategy to improve net fetal protein acccretion and fetal growth in IUGR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fetus with IUGR is able to use amino acids for protein synthesis when they are directly infused into the circulation, but the fetus with IGR is less able to use amino acid for oxidation, thus leading to increased protein accretions rates.

fetal growth restriction is associated with decreased fetal amino acid uptake, which is not corrected by increasing amino acid delivery to the fetal circulation, but rather by increasing insulin delivery.
amino acid infusion into the IUGR fetus increases net protein acccretion rates, but insulin infusion has no additional effect.
